title: Romans land at Empúries
description: A Roman army lands to cut Hannibal's supply lines, beginning two centuries of conquest of the peninsula.

title: Third Council of Toledo
description: King Reccared and the Visigoths give up Arian Christianity for the Catholic faith of their subjects.

title: Battle of Guadalete
description: A Muslim army from North Africa under Tariq ibn Ziyad defeats King Roderic, and most of the peninsula falls within a few years.

title: Battle of Covadonga
description: Pelagius defeats an Umayyad force in the mountains, later remembered as the start of the Reconquista; the year is uncertain.

title: Caliphate of Córdoba proclaimed
description: Abd al-Rahman III takes the title of caliph, at the height of Muslim Spain's power and learning.

title: Castile takes Toledo
description: Alfonso VI captures the old Visigothic capital, the first great Muslim city to fall to the Christian kingdoms.

title: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
description: The allied Christian kings break the Almohad army, after which most of the south is conquered within forty years.

title: Marriage of Ferdinand and Isabella
description: The marriage of the heirs of Aragon and Castile leads to the union of the two crowns.

title: Spanish Inquisition established
description: Pope Sixtus IV allows Ferdinand and Isabella to appoint inquisitors to pursue converts suspected of keeping their old faith.

title: Surrender of Granada
description: The last Muslim state in the peninsula surrenders to Ferdinand and Isabella.

title: Columbus reaches the Americas
description: Sailing west for Castile, Christopher Columbus lands on an island in the Bahamas.

title: Treaty of Tordesillas
description: Castile and Portugal divide the newly found lands outside Europe along a line in the Atlantic.

title: First voyage round the world completed
description: Juan Sebastián Elcano brings home one ship and eighteen men of the expedition Magellan had led out three years before.

title: Madrid becomes the capital
description: Philip II moves his court to Madrid.

title: Expulsion of the Moriscos
description: Philip III orders the descendants of Spain's Muslims to leave; early estimates put the number expelled at 275,000 to 300,000.

title: Battle of Rocroi
description: A French army defeats the Spanish infantry long thought unbeatable, a sign of Spain's decline as a military power.

title: Peace of Utrecht
description: The treaties that end the War of the Spanish Succession leave a Bourbon on the Spanish throne but give Gibraltar to Britain and Spain's Italian and Netherlandish lands to others.

title: Dos de Mayo Uprising
description: The people of Madrid rise against the French occupation, starting the Peninsular War.

title: Constitution of Cádiz
description: The Cortes, besieged by the French, adopts a liberal constitution that becomes a model in Spain and Latin America.

title: Battle of Ayacucho
description: The defeat of the last royalist army ends Spanish rule in South America.

title: Treaty of Paris
description: After defeat by the United States, Spain gives up Cuba and cedes Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines.

title: Second Republic proclaimed
description: After republican victories in municipal elections King Alfonso XIII leaves the country.

title: Military rising begins the Civil War
description: Army officers rebel against the Republic, starting in Spanish Morocco; the war lasts nearly three years.

title: Bombing of Guernica
description: German and Italian aircraft supporting Franco destroy the Basque town.

title: End of the Civil War
description: Franco declares victory, beginning a dictatorship of 36 years.

title: Death of Franco
description: Franco dies and Juan Carlos I becomes king, opening the transition to democracy.

title: Constitution approved
description: Voters approve a democratic constitution with a parliamentary monarchy and self-governing regions.

title: Attempted coup of 23 February
description: Civil Guards seize parliament, and the coup collapses after the king broadcasts his support for the constitution.

title: Spain joins the European Communities
description: Spain and Portugal become members.

title: Madrid train bombings
description: Bombs on commuter trains kill 193 people.
